body.statement: For every \(0<\rho<1\), the exact worst-instance multiplier within \(\mathfrak D_2\) is \[\inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\frac{\Gamma_{\rho,w}(\mu)}{I_w(\mu)}=\min\left\{\rho C,\ 1+(1-\rho)\eta\right\}.\] A best-elimination witness with \(h\in\arg\min_k C_k\) attains the first branch. For an \(e\in\arg\min_k w_k/(1-w_k)\), two distinct survivors and a sufficiently separated eliminated arm attain the second branch. Consequently \(\rho^\star\) uniquely maximizes the displayed value and the maximum is \(G\).
body.justification: Matching branch witnesses certify optimal timing rather than merely proposing a favorable first-batch fraction.
body.gap: Existing batched results optimize fixed-confidence sample or batch complexity, and existing adaptive large-deviation results give bounds; none evaluates this constrained heteroskedastic fixed-budget saddle value.
body.consumer: The theorem supplies a tuning rule that is minimax within the implementable proportional family and identifies which stress-test instance limits it.
